+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca` runs from any shell, not only an Orca terminal, and that the
+# skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, which outside the FHS env is
+# an Electron binary looking for the host's libraries. The skills are stubs
+# that tell the agent to run `orca skills get <name>`, so a skill without a
+# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
+# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
+# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
+# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# uname -n, not /etc/hostname: Orca's sandbox does not bind the latter in.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+drv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+  --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or "") == "orca-cli") ps)).drvPath') \
+  || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI"
+
+if [ -x "$CLI/bin/orca" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/orca"
+else fail "bin/orca" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's runScript
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+manifest=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  f="$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"; [ -f "$f" ] && echo "$f"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$manifest" ] || { echo "no skills manifest in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() { env $(env | grep -o '^ORCA_[A-Z_]*' | sed 's/^/-u /') PATH="$clean_path" "$@"; }
+
+want_version=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+  --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or "") == "orca-cli") ps)).version')
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# `skills list` reads the bundled guide table locally, no running app needed.
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" skills list --json 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '"orca-cli"'; then pass "orca skills list works outside Orca"
+else fail "orca skills list" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null 2>&1
+  want=$(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys
+for s in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["skills"]:
+  if s["name"]==sys.argv[2]:
+    print(next(f["exactSha256"] for f in s["files"] if f["path"]=="SKILL.md"))' "$manifest" "$s")
+  got=$(sha256sum "$src/SKILL.md" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)
+  if [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then pass "$s/SKILL.md matches this build's manifest"
+  else fail "$s" "SKILL.md sha256 '${got:-missing}', manifest wants '${want:-no entry}'"; fi
+done
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

     8	# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, which outside the FHS env is

    11	# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
    12	# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
    13	# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
    14	# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.
    15	#

    17	#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it

    20	set -o pipefail

    22	fails=0; n=0

    27	# uname -n, not /etc/hostname: Orca's sandbox does not bind the latter in.

    32	  --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or "") == "orca-cli") ps)).drvPath') \

    37	if [ -x "$CLI/bin/orca" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/orca"

    48	outside() { env $(env | grep -o '^ORCA_[A-Z_]*' | sed 's/^/-u /') PATH="$clean_path" "$@"; }
    49	
    50	want_version=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
    51	  --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or "") == "orca-cli") ps)).version')
    52	got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
    53	if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"

    56	# `skills list` reads the bundled guide table locally, no running app needed.
    57	got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" skills list --json 2>&1)
    58	if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '"orca-cli"'; then pass "orca skills list works outside Orca"
    59	else fail "orca skills list" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi

    61	for s in $SKILLS; do
    62	  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
    63	    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
    64	  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
    65	  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
    66	    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
    67	  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null 2>&1

    69	for s in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["skills"]:
    70	  if s["name"]==sys.argv[2]:
    71	    print(next(f["exactSha256"] for f in s["files"] if f["path"]=="SKILL.md"))' "$manifest" "$s")

    74	  else fail "$s" "SKILL.md sha256 '${got:-missing}', manifest wants '${want:-no entry}'"; fi
    75	done
    76	
    77	printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
    78	[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

None found.

**1. The six skills tell agents outside an Orca terminal to run `orca-ide`, not `orca`. In this config `orca-ide` is the GUI launcher.** (/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/orca-cli-skills/orca.nix:93-101, 134)

- The comment at orca.nix:93 says `orca` is "the name the skills and Orca's own terminals use". For non-Orca shells, which is exactly the case this change targets, that is wrong.
- `~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide` is `nixGLCombinedWrapper` running `orca-1.4.238/bin/orca-ide`. That is the AppRun/Electron GUI wrapper with `--ozone-platform=wayland`, not `resources/bin/orca-ide`, the node-mode CLI script.
- So an agent in a plain shell does as the skill says and runs `orca-ide skills get orca-cli`. It hits the GUI binary, which most likely starts or focuses the app instead of printing the guide (inferred; I did not run it). If `~/.local/bin` comes before the nix profile on PATH, it instead gets Orca's CliInstaller symlink to a raw store path — the very case the comment says this change avoids.
- The new `orca` binary is only reached when the skill's `ORCA_CLI_COMMAND` / `orca` branches apply. Inside Orca terminals the shim already handles those.
- Possible fixes:
  - Make the GUI's `orca-ide` wrapper dispatch: CLI subcommands go to the CLI script, no args or Electron flags go to AppRun.
  - Or export `ORCA_CLI_COMMAND=orca` session-wide. The skill checks that first, but upstream documents it as a WSL-only variable, so it may be fragile.
- Either way, fix the comment.

**2. The test does not exercise the path the skills actually take.** (/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/orca-cli-skills/tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:46-59)
- It runs `$CLI/bin/orca` by absolute path. The cleaned `PATH` therefore has no effect, and nothing checks what `orca` or `orca-ide` resolve to on PATH. The header's claim "that `orca` runs from any shell" is not tested.
- It tests `skills list` but never `skills get <name>`, which is the command every stub runs.
- A case that resolves `orca-ide` on a clean PATH and runs `skills get orca-cli` would have caught issue 1.

## Security
I found nothing at Critical or Important severity.
- **Pinning is strong.** The AppImage has a sha512 SRI hash. The skills source is pinned to a full 40-character rev plus a sha256 NAR hash. The test also checks each SKILL.md against the bundled `current-manifest.json` hashes.
- **The FHS env adds no new exposure.** `orcaCli` uses `appimageTools.defaultFhsEnvArgs` with no `extraBwrapArgs`, so the bwrap binds are the same stock buildFHSEnv set the GUI already gets. It is not a security boundary in either direction: $HOME, /run, /tmp and the network are shared.
- **Skill content: mostly benign stubs, with one prompt-level item worth knowing about** (nit). Each stub says: if a command fails with `runtime_access_denied`, "re-run it with escalated permissions". That pushes agents to ask for sandbox escalation for any Orca socket error.
  - `computer-use` lets agents drive arbitrary local GUI windows. It is now installed into every Claude session on desktop hosts, not just sessions inside Orca. It is scoped as last-resort, but enabling it is a deliberate choice; consider leaving it out of `orcaSkills`.
  - `orca-linear` / `linear-tickets` correctly treat ticket text as untrusted. `linear-tickets` duplicates `orca-linear` (it is the legacy name), so installing both is redundant.
- **The test does not leak secrets.** `outside()` (line 48) uses `grep -o '^ORCA_[A-Z_]*'`, so only variable names reach `env -u` as arguments. A multi-line env value whose second line starts with `ORCA_` would also match. Use `[A-Za-z0-9_]*`, or `compgen -e | grep '^ORCA_'`. The current variable names are all `[A-Z_]`, so nothing is broken today.
- **No email addresses or private data** in either file. The only `@` is `"$@"`. The hostname comes from `uname -n` at runtime, not hard-coded.

- **orca.nix:106: duplication.** `libsecret` is listed again here. The CLI runs with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` ("must never initialize Chromium"), so safeStorage and libsecret are probably not needed; drop it, or share one `extraPkgs` list with the GUI.
- **orca.nix:116-121: differs from repo convention.** Every other third-party skill in home.nix (2195-2203: `teach`, `security-audit`) comes from a flake input with a "Pinned via flake.lock; `nix flake update X` to bump" comment.

  - Directory-level symlinks match `teach` and `security-audit`, which is good.
- **orca.nix:122-125 and tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:29: the six skill names are listed twice.** The test could read them from `home.file` attribute names instead of keeping its own copy.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:31-33 and 50-51: two near-identical `nix eval` calls** filter `home.packages` for `orca-cli`. Fetch `drvPath` and `version` in one eval.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:26-28: inconsistent with tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.**
  - sandbox-fonts.sh uses `cat /etc/hostname` and accepts an optional built-path argument. The new test uses `uname -n` and takes no argument.
  - The `uname -n` comment is accurate: `/etc/hostname` is absent inside Orca's sandbox. But sandbox-fonts.sh is now the odd one out and will fail there, so consider aligning it.
  - Adding the same `<path>` argument would match the sibling's usage block.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:67:** `nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null 2>&1` swallows fetch errors. A failure only shows up later as "sha256 'missing'", which is misleading but harmless.
- **orca.nix:137-140:** `home.file` uses `lib.mkIf` while `home.packages` uses `lib.optionals`. Both work; `mkIf` is the more idiomatic choice for an attribute set, so this is fine.

## Security
I found nothing at Critical or Important severity.
- **Pinning is strong.** The AppImage has a sha512 SRI hash. The skills source is pinned to a full 40-character rev plus a sha256 NAR hash. The test also checks each SKILL.md against the bundled `current-manifest.json` hashes.
- **The FHS env adds no new exposure.** `orcaCli` uses `appimageTools.defaultFhsEnvArgs` with no `extraBwrapArgs`, so the bwrap binds are the same stock buildFHSEnv set the GUI already gets. It is not a security boundary in either direction: $HOME, /run, /tmp and the network are shared.
- **Skill content: mostly benign stubs, with one prompt-level item worth knowing about** (nit). Each stub says: if a command fails with `runtime_access_denied`, "re-run it with escalated permissions". That pushes agents to ask for sandbox escalation for any Orca socket error.
  - `computer-use` lets agents drive arbitrary local GUI windows. It is now installed into every Claude session on desktop hosts, not just sessions inside Orca. It is scoped as last-resort, but enabling it is a deliberate choice; consider leaving it out of `orcaSkills`.
  - `orca-linear` / `linear-tickets` correctly treat ticket text as untrusted. `linear-tickets` duplicates `orca-linear` (it is the legacy name), so installing both is redundant.
- **The test does not leak secrets.** `outside()` (line 48) uses `grep -o '^ORCA_[A-Z_]*'`, so only variable names reach `env -u` as arguments. Nothing is echoed, and `ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_TOKEN`'s value never appears. The only output is the CLI's own `--version` / `skills list` text in failure messages, plus store paths.
  - Robustness nit: the character class has no digits or lowercase. A future `ORCA_V2_X`-style name would only be partly matched, unsetting the wrong name and leaving the real variable set. A multi-line env value whose second line starts with `ORCA_` would also match. Use `[A-Za-z0-9_]*`, or `compgen -e | grep '^ORCA_'`. The current variable names are all `[A-Z_]`, so nothing is broken today.
- **No email addresses or private data** in either file. The only `@` is `"$@"`. The hostname comes from `uname -n` at runtime, not hard-coded.
